terms_note: Career portals *.breezy.hr with a public positions JSON; apply form web-only.

endpoints.call: the per-company public positions JSON (GET https://{company}.breezy.hr/json — live-verified on breezy.breezy.hr: id, friendly_id, name, url, published_date, type, location, department, salary, company
endpoints.notes: from the docs / live response read on 2026-09-05

endpoints.call: the documented Public API v3 (https://api.breezy.hr/v3, /signin → token, /company/{id}/positions, /company/{id}/position/{id}/candidates) is the EMPLOYER's account
endpoints.notes: from the docs / live response read on 2026-09-05

reference.limits: Not published on the pages opened. Breezy HR Public API requires signing in with a Breezy customer account (/signin returns the access token); positions / candidates endpoints act on the company's own data. The public careers JSON is not documented on developer.breezy.hr (guessed doc pages 404) — treat it as an undocumented courtesy endpoint. No terms text was readable (breezy.hr answered 202 with an empty body).

fields.name: api_token
fields.help: Breezy Personal Access Token (prefix breezy_pat_) from the Breezy app: user icon > My Settings > API Keys > Create API Key; sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. It acts as the Breezy user who created it.

config_fields.name: company_id
config_fields.help: The Breezy company id (12-14 character hex `_id` from GET /v3/companies) whose positions are read.

me.note: GET /v3/user returns the authenticated user (_id, email_address, name, username).

search.note: Employer ATS API: GET /v3/company/{company_id}/positions?state=published lists the configured company's OWN published positions (not a cross-company job search). There is no keyword or location filter, so query/location are not sent — filter client-side. Paging: page_size ('capped at 50') + page (1-based). id is the position _id (use it with get_posting); salary period is in raw.salary.period; department, type, experience, friendly_id and location.is_remote are in raw. There is no public posting URL field, so url is null.

get_posting.note: GET /v3/company/{company_id}/position/{position_id}: 'full details (name, type, state, location, department, description, application form configuration, salary range, custom attributes, and team/admin…)'.

not_offered.apply: The API is for the employer's own account: POST /company/{id}/position/{id}/candidates 'Creates a candidate on the specified position' as the recruiter (origin sourced/applied), which is not a job seeker applying; candidates apply on the company's Breezy careers page.
not_offered.list_messages: Candidate conversations are per candidate (GET /company/{id}/position/{id}/candidate/{id}/conversation needs both a position and a candidate id), so there is no single inbox call that fits list_messages(thread_id).
